1.2 Why the previous style is likely to plateau and what this plan changes

All-local improvement sequences based only on changing one positive and one negative coordinate define very sparse directions. Such a move can reduce one active lag while raising another, and the allowed line itself is usually too narrow to require coordinated shifts of many levels even though all lags are coupled. The proposed method deliberately introduces dense coordinated motions.

The main new engine is a smoothed-max, tangent-projected descent with exact one-dimensional descent along dense directions. The current correlation vector gives a smooth log-sum-exp weight over all active lags. Its gradient gives a dense, feasible tangent direction. Along that direction, the actual updated objective is exactly known as a max of quadratic slices. The search then chooses the best true line move and accepts it only after re-evaluating the original finite-support score. This is materially different from single transfer/pair moves, pure binary search, or a hand-designed linear active-set direction: it discovers a dense direction by smoothed weights and keeps the acceptance entirely tied to the actual evaluator.

A secondary contribution is a diversified combinatorial stream. Before dense descent needs polished combinatorial skeleton sequences at potentially several n values. The combinatorial stage should use exact correlations directly from the binary states and can transfer a robust skeleton back to the continuous dense stage. Small resolutions are preferred for speed but are retained only when the exact score supports them. If this stage fails, the program still relies on the parent and dense descent.

It uses an adaptive log-sum exponential surrogate over all correlations, generates dense descent directions from its smooth gradient, performs exact pure-line evaluation of the original bilinear function, and has several global diversification classes.
